title: परदेशमा पराइको आत्मीयता, आफ्नैको परायापन
content:
परदेशको जीवन बाहिरबाट हेर्दा जति आकर्षक देखिन्छ, भित्रबाट त्यति नै सङ्घर्षपूर्ण हुन्छ । उज्यालो सहर, व्यवस्थित सडक, सुविधासम्पन्न यातायात र राम्रो कमाइका कथाले धेरैलाई विदेश आउन आकर्षित गर्छन् । तर यहाँ आइपुगेपछि मात्रै थाहा हुन्छ । परदेशको वास्तविक जीवन कमाइ र सुविधामा मात्र सीमित हुँदैन । यससँगै जोडिएका हुन्छन् एक्लोपन, पारिवारिक विछोड, भाषाको समस्या, कामको दबाब र आफ्नोपनको खोजी । जापानका विभिन्न सहरमा रहेका नेपालीहरूको जीवन पनि यस्तै अनुभवले भरिएको छ। कोही परिवारको भविष्य बनाउन आएका छन्, कोही आफ्नो सपना पूरा गर्न त कोही घरको आर्थिक अवस्था सुधार्ने जिम्मेवारी बोकेर परदेशिएका छन्। सबैका आफ्ना फरक फरक उद्देश्य हुन सक्छन् । तर सङ्घर्षका धेरै कथा भने उस्तै मिल्दाजुल्दा छन् । परदेशमा मानिसलाई सबैभन्दा बढी अभाव केको हुन्छ ? पैसा, सुविधा वा अवसरको ? यी सबै आवश्यक छन् । तर लामो समय परदेशमा बिताएका धेरै मानिसका अनुभव सुन्दा एउटा कुरा बुझिन्छ कहिलेकाहीँ मानिसलाई पैसाभन्दा बढी आफ्नोपनको आवश्यकता पर्दो रहेछ । कामबाट थाकेर फर्किएपछि दुई शब्द मन खोलेर बोल्न सक्ने साथी, अप्ठ्यारो पर्दा सहयोग गर्ने सहकर्मी र आफूलाई बुझिदिने एउटा मान्छे नै ठूलो सहारा बन्नसक्छ ।यस्तो आत्मीयता सधैँ आफ्नै देशका मानिसबाट मात्रै प्राप्त हुन्छ भन्ने पनि छैन । कहिलेकाहीँ फरक भाषा, संस्कृति र देशको मानिसले पनि आफ्नै परिवारको सदस्यले जस्तै माया र सद्भाव दिनसक्छ । जापानमा सँगै काम गरेका विभिन्न देशका साथीहरूसँग बनेका सम्बन्धले पनि धेरै नेपालीलाई यस्तो अनुभव गराएको छ। छोटो समयको सहकार्यले पनि जीवनभर सम्झनलायक सम्बन्ध बन्न सक्छन् । तर अर्कोतर्फ, आफ्नै देशका मानिससँग अपेक्षा गरिएको आत्मीयता नपाउँदा मन दुख्ने अनुभव पनि कम छैन । विशेषगरी नयाँ आएका नेपालीहरूले भाषा, काम र यहाँको नियमकानुन बुझ्न धेरै कठिनाइ भोगिरहेका हुन्छन् । यस्तो अवस्थामा पहिले नै जापानमा बसेका नेपालीबाट सहयोग, सद्भाव र मार्गदर्शनको अपेक्षा गर्नु स्वाभाविक हो । दुःखको कुरा, कतिपय अवस्थामा नयाँ आउनेलाई सहयोग गर्नुको सट्टा हेप्ने, सानो देखाउने, आफ्नो अनुभवको घमण्ड गर्ने र आफूलाई अरूभन्दा ठूलो ठान्ने प्रवृत्ति पनि देखिन्छ। आफू पनि कुनै दिन नयाँ भएर आएको कुरा बिर्सेर अरूको कठिनाइलाई सामान्य ठान्ने व्यवहारले नेपालीबीचको सम्बन्धलाई कमजोर बनाउँछ । हामी सबैले बुझ्नुपर्ने कुरा के हो भने जापानमा धेरै वर्ष बिताउँदैमा कोही ठूलो हुँदैन । अनुभवको वास्तविक मूल्य अरूलाई दबाउन होइन, बाटो देखाउन सक्नुमा हुन्छ। आफूले भोगेका कठिनाइबाट सिकेका कुरा नयाँ आउनेलाई सिकाउन सक्नु, काम र जीवनका अप्ठ्यारामा साथ दिन सक्नु र कसैलाई परदेशमा एक्लो महसुस हुन नदिनु नै अनुभवको सही उपयोग हो जस्तो मलाई लाग्छ । हिजो हामी पनि नयाँ थियौँ । हामीलाई पनि कसैले बाटो देखाइदिएको थियो, कसैले काम सिकाइदिएको थियो, कसैले अप्ठ्यारोमा सहयोग गरेको थियो। आज हामीले पाएको त्यो सहयोग र सद्भाव भोलि अर्को नयाँ व्यक्तिसम्म पुर्‍याउन सक्नुपर्छ । अर्को महत्त्वपूर्ण कुरा, परदेशमा सबैको जीवन सहज छैन । बाहिरबाट राम्रो कमाइ गरिरहेको देखिने मानिस पनि भित्रभित्रै ऋण, पारिवारिक जिम्मेवारी, सम्बन्धको दूरी र भविष्यको चिन्ताले थिचिएको हुनसक्छ । त्यसैले कसैको अवस्था नबुझी उसको संघर्षलाई कमजोर ठान्नु हुँदैन। हामीले देख्ने मानिसको अनुहार हो, उसले बोकेको पीडा होइन । परदेशमा पैसा कमाउनु, राम्रो काम पाउनु र परिवारका आवश्यकता पूरा गर्नु निश्चय नै महत्त्वपूर्ण उपलब्धि हुन्। तर त्यससँगै मानवीय सम्बन्ध जोगाउनु, अरूको सम्मान गर्नु र आफूले पनि कसैलाई आत्मीयता दिन सक्नु उत्तिकै महत्त्वपूर्ण छ । हामी विदेशमा आफ्नो भविष्य बनाउन आएका हौँ । तर त्यस क्रममा आफ्नो संस्कार र मानवीयता गुमाउनु हुँदैन । नेपाली हुनुको अर्थ केवल एउटै भाषा बोल्नु वा एउटै देशबाट आउनु मात्र होइन, दुःखमा साथ दिनु, सुखमा खुसी साट्नु र अप्ठ्यारोमा एकअर्काको हात समात्नु पनि हो । अन्ततः परदेशमा पराइ पनि आफ्ना बन्न सक्छन् र आफ्नै भएर पनि कोही पराइ बन्न सक्छन् । सम्बन्धको वास्तविक आधार राष्ट्रियता, भाषा वा बसाइको अवधि होइन, व्यवहार र आत्मीयता रहेछ । हामी जहाँ रहे पनि कम्तीमा एउटा यस्तो संस्कार विकास गर्न सकौँ आफूले भोगेको दुःख अरूलाई नदिऔँ, आफूले पाएको सहयोग अरूलाई पनि बाँडौँ र परदेशमा कसैलाई आफ्नै देशको मान्छे भएर पनि एक्लो महसुस हुन नदिऔँ। किनकि परदेशमा कमाएको पैसाले घरको आवश्यकता पूरा होला, तर मान्छेले दिएको आत्मीयताले मात्रै मनको खालीपन भरिन सक्छ । (गंगादेव गाउँपालिका ६ रोल्पाका केसी हाल जापानकाे साइतमा बस्दै आएका छन् ।) Life abroad may seem attractive from the outside, but it is a struggle from the inside. Bright cities, well-organized roads, convenient transportation, and stories of good earnings attract many to come abroad. But you only realize it when you arrive here. The real life abroad is not limited to earnings and convenience. Along with this, loneliness, family separation, language problems, work pressure, and the search for belonging are also associated with it. The lives of Nepalis living in various cities in Japan are also filled with similar experiences. Some have come to build a future for their families, some to fulfill their dreams, and some have gone abroad with the responsibility of improving the financial situation of their homes. Everyone may have their own different goals. But many of the stories of struggle are similar. What do people lack the most in a foreign country? Money, convenience or opportunity? All of these are necessary. But when you listen to the experiences of many people who have spent a long time abroad, you understand one thing: sometimes people need belonging more than money. A friend who can speak a few words openly after returning from work, a colleague who helps you when you are in trouble, and a person who understands you can be a great support. Such intimacy is not always obtained only from people in your own country. Sometimes, people of different languages, cultures and countries can give love and goodwill like members of your own family. The relationships formed with friends from different countries who worked together in Japan have also given many Nepalis this experience. Even short-term collaborations can create relationships that will be remembered for a lifetime. But on the other hand, not getting the expected intimacy with the people of one's own country is also a heartbreaking experience. Especially, newly arrived Nepalis face a lot of difficulties in understanding the language, work, and the rules and regulations here. In such a situation, it is natural to expect support, goodwill, and guidance from Nepalis who have already settled in Japan. Sadly, in some cases, instead of helping newcomers, there is a tendency to belittle, belittle, boast about one's own experience, and consider oneself superior to others. This behavior of forgetting that one too was a newcomer and considering the difficulties of others as normal weakens relations between Nepalis. What we all need to understand is that spending many years in Japan does not make anyone great. The real value of experience is not in suppressing others, but in being able to show the way. I think the right use of experience is to be able to teach newcomers what you have learned from your own hardships, to be able to support them in the difficulties of work and life, and to prevent anyone from feeling alone in a foreign country. Yesterday we were new too. Someone had shown us the way, someone had taught us a job, someone had helped us in times of trouble. We should be able to pass on the support and goodwill we received today to another new person tomorrow. Another important thing is that not everyone's life is easy abroad. Even someone who appears to be earning well on the outside may be burdened with debt, family responsibilities, distance in relationships, and worries about the future. Therefore, we should not consider someone's struggle as weak without understanding their situation. What we see is the face of the person, not the pain they carry. Earning money abroad, getting a good job, and providing for your family are certainly important achievements. But it is equally important to maintain human relationships, respect others, and be able to give intimacy to someone. We have come abroad to build our future. But in the process, we should not lose our culture and humanity. Being Nepali does not only mean speaking the same language or coming from the same country, but also supporting each other in times of sorrow, sharing joy in times of happiness, and holding each other's hands in times of difficulty. Ultimately, even strangers in a foreign country can become our own, and even those who are our own can become strangers. The real basis of relationships is not nationality, language, or length of stay, but behavior and intimacy. Wherever we live, we can at least develop such a culture that we do not give the pain we experience to others, share the help we receive with others, and do not let anyone feel lonely abroad, even if they are a person from our own country. Because the money earned abroad may fulfill the needs of the home, but only the intimacy given by people can fill the emptiness of the heart. (KC from Gangadev Rural Municipality-6, Rolpa is currently living in Japan.)

संघर्षलाई कमजोर ठान्नु हुँदैन। हामीले देख्ने मानिसको अनुहार हो, उसले बोकेको पीडा होइन । परदेशमा पैसा कमाउनु, राम्रो काम पाउनु र परिवारका आवश्यकता पूरा गर्नु निश्चय नै महत्त्वपूर्ण उपलब्धि हुन्। तर त्यससँगै मानवीय सम्बन्ध जोगाउनु, अरूको सम्मान गर्नु र आफूले पनि कसैलाई आत्मीयता दिन सक्नु उत्तिकै महत्त्वपूर्ण छ । हामी विदेशमा आफ्नो भविष्य बनाउन आएका हौँ । तर त्यस क्रममा आफ्नो संस्कार र मानवीयता गुमाउनु हुँदैन । नेपाली हुनुको अर्थ केवल एउटै भाषा बोल्नु वा एउटै देशबाट आउनु मात्र होइन, दुःखमा साथ दिनु, सुखमा खुसी साट्नु र अप्ठ्यारोमा एकअर्काको हात समात्नु पनि हो । अन्ततः परदेशमा पराइ पनि आफ्ना बन्न सक्छन् र आफ्नै भएर पनि कोही पराइ बन्न सक्छन् । सम्बन्धको वास्तविक आधार राष्ट्रियता, भाषा वा बसाइको अवधि होइन, व्यवहार र आत्मीयता रहेछ । हामी जहाँ रहे पनि कम्तीमा एउटा यस्तो संस्कार विकास गर्न सकौँ आफूले भोगेको दुःख अरूलाई नदिऔँ, आफूले पाएको सहयोग अरूलाई पनि बाँडौँ र परदेशमा कसैलाई आफ्नै देशको मान्छे भएर पनि एक्लो महसुस हुन नदिऔँ। किनकि परदेशमा कमाएको पैसाले घरको आवश्यकता पूरा होला, तर मान्छेले दिएको आत्मीयताले मात्रै मनको खालीपन भरिन सक्छ । (गंगादेव गाउँपालिका ६ रोल्पाका केसी हाल जापानकाे साइतमा बस्दै आएका छन् ।)

परदेशको जीवन बाहिरबाट हेर्दा जति आकर्षक देखिन्छ, भित्रबाट त्यति नै सङ्घर्षपूर्ण हुन्छ । उज्यालो सहर, व्यवस्थित सडक, सुविधासम्पन्न यातायात र राम्रो कमाइका कथाले धेरैलाई विदेश आउन आकर्षित गर्छन् । तर यहाँ आइपुगेपछि मात्रै थाहा हुन्छ । परदेशको वास्तविक जीवन कमाइ र सुविधामा मात्र सीमित हुँदैन । यससँगै जोडिएका हुन्छन् एक्लोपन, पारिवारिक विछोड, भाषाको समस्या, कामको दबाब र आफ्नोपनको खोजी ।

जापानका विभिन्न सहरमा रहेका नेपालीहरूको जीवन पनि यस्तै अनुभवले भरिएको छ। कोही परिवारको भविष्य बनाउन आएका छन्, कोही आफ्नो सपना पूरा गर्न त कोही घरको आर्थिक अवस्था सुधार्ने जिम्मेवारी बोकेर परदेशिएका छन्। सबैका आफ्ना फरक फरक उद्देश्य हुन सक्छन् । तर सङ्घर्षका धेरै कथा भने उस्तै मिल्दाजुल्दा छन् ।

परदेशमा मानिसलाई सबैभन्दा बढी अभाव केको हुन्छ ? पैसा, सुविधा वा अवसरको ? यी सबै आवश्यक छन् । तर लामो समय परदेशमा बिताएका धेरै मानिसका अनुभव सुन्दा एउटा कुरा बुझिन्छ कहिलेकाहीँ मानिसलाई पैसाभन्दा बढी आफ्नोपनको आवश्यकता पर्दो रहेछ । कामबाट थाकेर फर्किएपछि दुई शब्द मन खोलेर बोल्न सक्ने साथी, अप्ठ्यारो पर्दा सहयोग गर्ने सहकर्मी र आफूलाई बुझिदिने एउटा मान्छे नै ठूलो सहारा बन्नसक्छ ।यस्तो आत्मीयता सधैँ आफ्नै देशका मानिसबाट मात्रै प्राप्त हुन्छ भन्ने पनि छैन । कहिलेकाहीँ फरक भाषा, संस्कृति र देशको मानिसले पनि आफ्नै परिवारको सदस्यले जस्तै माया र सद्भाव दिनसक्छ । जापानमा सँगै काम गरेका विभिन्न देशका साथीहरूसँग बनेका सम्बन्धले पनि धेरै नेपालीलाई यस्तो अनुभव गराएको छ। छोटो समयको सहकार्यले पनि जीवनभर सम्झनलायक सम्बन्ध बन्न सक्छन् ।

तर अर्कोतर्फ, आफ्नै देशका मानिससँग अपेक्षा गरिएको आत्मीयता नपाउँदा मन दुख्ने अनुभव पनि कम छैन । विशेषगरी नयाँ आएका नेपालीहरूले भाषा, काम र यहाँको नियमकानुन बुझ्न धेरै कठिनाइ भोगिरहेका हुन्छन् । यस्तो अवस्थामा पहिले नै जापानमा बसेका नेपालीबाट सहयोग, सद्भाव र मार्गदर्शनको अपेक्षा गर्नु स्वाभाविक हो ।

दुःखको कुरा, कतिपय अवस्थामा नयाँ आउनेलाई सहयोग गर्नुको सट्टा हेप्ने, सानो देखाउने, आफ्नो अनुभवको घमण्ड गर्ने र आफूलाई अरूभन्दा ठूलो ठान्ने प्रवृत्ति पनि देखिन्छ। आफू पनि कुनै दिन नयाँ भएर आएको कुरा बिर्सेर अरूको कठिनाइलाई सामान्य ठान्ने व्यवहारले नेपालीबीचको सम्बन्धलाई कमजोर बनाउँछ ।

हामी सबैले बुझ्नुपर्ने कुरा के हो भने जापानमा धेरै वर्ष बिताउँदैमा कोही ठूलो हुँदैन । अनुभवको वास्तविक मूल्य अरूलाई दबाउन होइन, बाटो देखाउन सक्नुमा हुन्छ। आफूले भोगेका कठिनाइबाट सिकेका कुरा नयाँ आउनेलाई सिकाउन सक्नु, काम र जीवनका अप्ठ्यारामा साथ दिन सक्नु र कसैलाई परदेशमा एक्लो महसुस हुन नदिनु नै अनुभवको सही उपयोग हो जस्तो मलाई लाग्छ ।

हिजो हामी पनि नयाँ थियौँ । हामीलाई पनि कसैले बाटो देखाइदिएको थियो, कसैले काम सिकाइदिएको थियो, कसैले अप्ठ्यारोमा सहयोग गरेको थियो। आज हामीले पाएको त्यो सहयोग र सद्भाव भोलि अर्को नयाँ व्यक्तिसम्म पुर्‍याउन सक्नुपर्छ ।

अर्को महत्त्वपूर्ण कुरा, परदेशमा सबैको जीवन सहज छैन । बाहिरबाट राम्रो कमाइ गरिरहेको देखिने मानिस पनि भित्रभित्रै ऋण, पारिवारिक जिम्मेवारी, सम्बन्धको दूरी र भविष्यको चिन्ताले थिचिएको हुनसक्छ । त्यसैले कसैको अवस्था नबुझी उसको संघर्षलाई कमजोर ठान्नु हुँदैन। हामीले देख्ने मानिसको अनुहार हो, उसले बोकेको पीडा होइन ।

परदेशमा पैसा कमाउनु, राम्रो काम पाउनु र परिवारका आवश्यकता पूरा गर्नु निश्चय नै महत्त्वपूर्ण उपलब्धि हुन्। तर त्यससँगै मानवीय सम्बन्ध जोगाउनु, अरूको सम्मान गर्नु र आफूले पनि कसैलाई आत्मीयता दिन सक्नु उत्तिकै महत्त्वपूर्ण छ ।

हामी विदेशमा आफ्नो भविष्य बनाउन आएका हौँ । तर त्यस क्रममा आफ्नो संस्कार र मानवीयता गुमाउनु हुँदैन । नेपाली हुनुको अर्थ केवल एउटै भाषा बोल्नु वा एउटै देशबाट आउनु मात्र होइन, दुःखमा साथ दिनु, सुखमा खुसी साट्नु र अप्ठ्यारोमा एकअर्काको हात समात्नु पनि हो ।

अन्ततः परदेशमा पराइ पनि आफ्ना बन्न सक्छन् र आफ्नै भएर पनि कोही पराइ बन्न सक्छन् । सम्बन्धको वास्तविक आधार राष्ट्रियता, भाषा वा बसाइको अवधि होइन, व्यवहार र आत्मीयता रहेछ । हामी जहाँ रहे पनि कम्तीमा एउटा यस्तो संस्कार विकास गर्न सकौँ आफूले भोगेको दुःख अरूलाई नदिऔँ, आफूले पाएको सहयोग अरूलाई पनि बाँडौँ र परदेशमा कसैलाई आफ्नै देशको मान्छे भएर पनि एक्लो महसुस हुन नदिऔँ। किनकि परदेशमा कमाएको पैसाले घरको आवश्यकता पूरा होला, तर मान्छेले दिएको आत्मीयताले मात्रै मनको खालीपन भरिन सक्छ ।

(गंगादेव गाउँपालिका ६ रोल्पाका केसी हाल जापानकाे साइतमा बस्दै आएका छन् ।)

Life abroad may seem attractive from the outside, but it is a struggle from the inside. Bright cities, well-organized roads, convenient transportation, and stories of good earnings attract many to come abroad. But you only realize it when you arrive here. The real life abroad is not limited to earnings and convenience. Along with this, loneliness, family separation, language problems, work pressure, and the search for belonging are also associated with it. The lives of Nepalis living in various cities in Japan are also filled with similar experiences. Some have come to build a future for their families, some to fulfill their dreams, and some have gone abroad with the responsibility of improving the financial situation of their homes. Everyone may have their own different goals. But many of the stories of struggle are similar. What do people lack the most in a foreign country? Money, convenience or opportunity? All of these are necessary. But when you listen to the experiences of many people who have spent a long time abroad, you understand one thing: sometimes people need belonging more than money. A friend who can speak a few words openly after returning from work, a colleague who helps you when you are in trouble, and a person who understands you can be a great support. Such intimacy is not always obtained only from people in your own country. Sometimes, people of different languages, cultures and countries can give love and goodwill like members of your own family. The relationships formed with friends from different countries who worked together in Japan have also given many Nepalis this experience. Even short-term collaborations can create relationships that will be remembered for a lifetime. But on the other hand, not getting the expected intimacy with the people of one's own country is also a heartbreaking experience. Especially, newly arrived Nepalis face a lot of difficulties in understanding the language, work, and the rules and regulations here. In such a situation, it is natural to expect support, goodwill, and guidance from Nepalis who have already settled in Japan. Sadly, in some cases, instead of helping newcomers, there is a tendency to belittle, belittle, boast about one's own experience, and consider oneself superior to others. This behavior of forgetting that one too was a newcomer and considering the difficulties of others as normal weakens relations between Nepalis. What we all need to understand is that spending many years in Japan does not make anyone great. The real value of experience is not in suppressing others, but in being able to show the way. I think the right use of experience is to be able to teach newcomers what you have learned from your own hardships, to be able to support them in the difficulties of work and life, and to prevent anyone from feeling alone in a foreign country. Yesterday we were new too. Someone had shown us the way, someone had taught us a job, someone had helped us in times of trouble. We should be able to pass on the support and goodwill we received today to another new person tomorrow. Another important thing is that not everyone's life is easy abroad. Even someone who appears to be earning well on the outside may be burdened with debt, family responsibilities, distance in relationships, and worries about the future. Therefore, we should not consider someone's struggle as weak without understanding their situation. What we see is the face of the person, not the pain they carry. Earning money abroad, getting a good job, and providing for your family are certainly important achievements. But it is equally important to maintain human relationships, respect others, and be able to give intimacy to someone. We have come abroad to build our future. But in the process, we should not lose our culture and humanity. Being Nepali does not only mean speaking the same language or coming from the same country, but also supporting each other in times of sorrow, sharing joy in times of happiness, and holding each other's hands in times of difficulty. Ultimately, even strangers in a foreign country can become our own, and even those who are our own can become strangers. The real basis of relationships is not nationality, language, or length of stay, but behavior and intimacy. Wherever we live, we can at least develop such a culture that we do not give the pain we experience to others, share the help we receive with others, and do not let anyone feel lonely abroad, even if they are a person from our own country. Because the money earned abroad may fulfill the needs of the home, but only the intimacy given by people can fill the emptiness of the heart. (KC from Gangadev Rural Municipality-6, Rolpa is currently living in Japan.)
